plain: First, check whether any windows, a back door, or a sliding door are unlocked, since people often forget these. Ask a trusted neighbor, your landlord, or the building manager whether they keep a spare key on file, since many apartment buildings do. If your door has a smart lock or keypad, try the backup code or the companion app before anything else. A locksmith can usually pick or drill a standard deadbolt within minutes, often for less than you would expect. As a last resort, call your building's emergency maintenance line or property management, since they may hold a master key. Afterward, consider leaving a spare key with a friend or neighbor for next time.

plain: Traditional Lebanese tabbouleh is mostly a fresh herb salad rather than a grain dish, so parsley is the star. You will need a large bunch of finely chopped flat-leaf parsley, a smaller amount of fresh mint, tomatoes diced small, finely chopped white or green onion, and just a few tablespoons of fine bulgur wheat, soaked briefly in water. Dress it with fresh lemon juice, good olive oil, and salt to taste; some cooks add a pinch of allspice or cinnamon. The bulgur should be a minor component, not the base, and everything is chopped very fine by hand. Serve it chilled, scooped up with lettuce leaves or pita.

plain: A batsman in cricket can be dismissed in several ways. The most common is bowled, when the ball hits the stumps directly from the bowler. Caught happens when a fielder catches the ball before it touches the ground after the batsman hits it. Leg before wicket (LBW) applies when the ball would have hit the stumps but is blocked by the batsman's body. Run out occurs when a fielder breaks the stumps while the batsman is out of their crease running between wickets, and stumped is similar but done by the wicketkeeper while the batsman is out of the crease but not running. Less common dismissals include hit wicket, handled the ball, obstructing the field, and timed out.

plain: There are several easy ways to add heat to pho. Sriracha stirred directly into the broth is the simplest option and lets you control the intensity. Thinly sliced fresh Thai chilies (bird's eye chilies) added to the bowl bring a sharper, more immediate heat than sauce. Chili oil or chili crisp drizzled on top adds both spice and a toasty flavor. A spoonful of sambal oelek gives heat with some texture from the crushed chilies. You can also steep dried chili flakes directly in the hot broth for a few minutes before serving so the heat infuses evenly. Combining two of these, like chili oil plus fresh sliced chilies, gives good depth without overwhelming the other flavors.

plain: The first ten amendments to the United States Constitution are collectively known as the Bill of Rights. They were ratified in 1791 and guarantee fundamental protections such as freedom of speech, religion, and the press (First Amendment), the right to bear arms (Second), protection against unreasonable searches and seizures (Fourth), the right to due process and against self-incrimination (Fifth), the right to a speedy trial by jury (Sixth), and protection against cruel and unusual punishment (Eighth). They were added shortly after the Constitution's ratification to address concerns that the original document did not sufficiently protect individual liberties from the federal government.

plain: A boat floats because of buoyancy: an object floats when it displaces a weight of water equal to its own weight, a principle discovered by Archimedes. Even though steel is much denser than water, a boat's hull is shaped hollow, enclosing a large volume of air. This means the boat's overall average density, including all that empty space, is lower than the density of water, so it floats. A solid block of steel of the same weight would sink because it has no hollow space and displaces far less water relative to its weight. Objects sink when their average density is greater than water's; they float when it's less, or when the water they push aside weighs as much as they do.

plain: While a putter is the standard tool for putting, other clubs can work in a pinch, especially just off the green. A low-lofted iron, such as a 7-, 8-, or 9-iron, can be used with a putting-style stroke for a 'bump and run' when the ball is just off the green through short fringe or fairway grass, letting it roll like a putt after a brief hop. A hybrid club can serve a similar purpose from slightly rougher lies, since its wider sole glides through grass without digging in. Some golfers even use a wedge with a putting stroke on very short chips. None of these substitute perfectly for a putter's face and weighting, but they get the job done from awkward spots near the green.

plain: The motto of the United States Marine Corps is 'Semper Fidelis,' a Latin phrase meaning 'Always Faithful' (often shortened to 'Semper Fi').
